learn.title: Learn
learn.lead: How Bros works, in plain words.
learn.windowSummary: Two minutes, one price, no race.
learn.graduationSummary: 25 people and a full credit goal.
learn.risksSummary: What can go wrong, said plainly.

window: Every launch on Bros starts with an opening window that lasts 120 seconds. Nobody can trade during it. Instead, people deposit Season Credit.

When the window closes, all deposits are treated as one buy. Everyone pays the same clearing price and gets tokens in proportion to what they put in. Arriving first doesn't help, so bots gain nothing by being fast.

During the window and for 10 minutes after it, only verified wallets can buy, each up to a cap: 50 SC at tier 1 and 125 SC at tier 2. The creator's own opening order sits in the same window and pays the same price.

You can set a limit price when you deposit. If the window clears above your limit, your whole deposit comes back. After settlement you claim your tokens, or they're claimed for you on your next trade.
graduation: Before graduation, a token trades on a bonding curve: its price follows a fixed formula, rising as people buy and falling as they sell.
A token graduates when two goals are met: its credit goal of 2,500 SC is full, and 25 different verified people have bought it. One big wallet can't graduate a token alone.
When the credit goal is full, buying pauses until someone sells. Selling always stays open. If 25 people haven't arrived 24 hours after the goal filled, the token can graduate anyway.

Anyone can press the graduate button and earn a small keeper bounty. At graduation, tokens and credit move into a pool that can never be withdrawn, and the creator's locked tokens start being released over 30 days. Graduation is not an endorsement.
seasonCredit: On testnet you trade with Season Credit (SC), a practice currency. It can't be sent to other wallets and has no monetary value.
Verified people claim credit once a day: 20 SC at tier 1 and 50 SC at tier 2. Missed days add up for at most 7 days. Tier 0 wallets can look around but can't claim.
Selling tokens returns SC, so active traders recycle it. Unspent credit burns when the season ends. Seasons last four weeks.

Points reward counterparties, holding, creator quality and curation, and give zero for transaction count, volume or launches. Points and badges have no monetary value and imply no future token or airdrop.
fees: Every trade pays a 1% fee, before and after graduation. 40% goes to the creator, 30% to holders and 30% to the protocol.
A creator can add a creator tax of 0 to 3%. It's printed on the Fairness Card, so you see it before you buy.
Launching costs 1 SC on testnet. Keepers who settle windows or graduate tokens earn a bounty of 0.05% of the amount moved, paid from the protocol share.
Holder rewards are paid in daily epochs. Fees are claimed when you ask for them; nothing is sent to you automatically.
risks: Bros is a testnet. Nothing here has monetary value, but the risks below are the same ones you'd face on mainnet, so read them as if it mattered.
Bros is non-custodial and cannot reverse transactions, freeze tokens, or recover keys. Every parameter change is announced at least 48 hours before it can run.

glossary.window: The first two minutes of every launch. Everyone who joins pays the same price when it closes, so being fastest doesn't help.
glossary.humansFirst: For the first minutes, only verified wallets can join, with a cap per person.
glossary.verified: Your wallet holds a Dojang attestation. Tier 1 comes from the GIWA faucet, tier 2 from an Upbit-verified address.
glossary.curve: Before graduation, the price follows a fixed formula: it rises as people buy and falls as they sell.
glossary.people: A token needs 25 different verified people holding it, plus enough credit, to graduate.
glossary.graduation: When a token meets both goals it moves to a pool that can never be withdrawn. Graduation is not an endorsement.
glossary.fairness: Six facts about a launch, read from the chain: creator share and lock, creator tax, window result, people needed, where fees go, team wallets.
glossary.tax: An optional extra fee of 0 to 3% that goes to the creator on every trade. It's printed on the Fairness Card.
glossary.fee: 1% of each trade. 40% goes to the creator, 30% to holders, 30% to the protocol.
glossary.slippage: How much worse than the quote you'll accept if the price moves before your trade lands. If it moves more, nothing is spent.
glossary.impact: How much your own trade moves the price. Big trades in small pools move it more.
glossary.credit: Practice currency for this testnet season. You get a daily amount by tier. It can't be sent to others and has no monetary value.
glossary.rewards: A share of trade fees paid daily to people holding the token.
glossary.vesting: The creator's tokens stay locked until graduation, then are released bit by bit over 30 days.
glossary.keeper: Anyone who presses the button that settles a window or graduates a token. They earn a small bounty.
glossary.clearing: The single price everyone in the window pays, known when the window closes.
glossary.team: A wallet the creator declared as theirs. Its trades are labelled so you can see them.
